Decision IC: on the 30 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of 0.013 with the next five days' returns (IC IR 0.09, t = 0.5, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 47 decision days had a mean rank IC of 0.007 with the next five days' returns (t = 0.3, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.32 (t 9.9), size -0.05 (t -1.4), growth -0.13 (t -2.4), momentum 0.06 (t 2.6); together they explain 59% of the daily variation (R²).
Of the -8.6% a year it earned over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market -6.2%, growth +2.3%, momentum +0.5%, size +0.1%; the alpha left is -5.2% a year (t = -0.9, within noise).
Verdict: the exposures account for -3.3% a year of it, and the -5.2% a year left over is not significant: one period of daily returns cannot tell it from luck.
P&L: -$7,184 in all, -$7,927 from 49 positions and +$743 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$404, 7 positions); 11-20 days the least (-$3,947, 8 positions).
By sector: Health Care made the most (+$1,855, 11 positions); Technology the least (-$3,815, 9 positions).
By stock: ABBV made the most (+$1,281, 2 positions); NEE the least (-$1,659, 4 positions).

News: 8 positions opened on news made +$229, the other 41 -$8,156; 6 positions closed on news made -$742; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys beat SPY by 0.27% (t 0.6).

Concentration: the positions lost -$7,927 in all; the best was DE bought 2022-11-03 and sold 2022-12-23, +$1,278. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned -8.5% instead of -7.2%.
